arxiv-2012-15148.title: Wigner–Weyl description of massless Dirac plasmas
arxiv-2012-15148.creator: José L. Figueiredo, João P. S. Bizarro, Hugo Terças
arxiv-2012-15148.description: Abstract We derive a quantum kinetic model describing the dynamics of graphene electrons in phase space based on the Wigner–Weyl formalism. To take into account the quantum nature of the carriers, we make use of the quantum Liouville equation for the density matrix.

arxiv-2301-09263.title: On the solutions of x 2 = B ​ y p + C ​ z p x^{2}=By^{p}+Cz^{p} and 2 ​ x 2 = B ​ y p + C ​ z p 2x^{2}=By^{p}+Cz^{p} over totally real fields
arxiv-2301-09263.creator: Narasimha Kumar, Satyabrat Sahoo
arxiv-2301-09263.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Narasimha Kumar, Satyabrat Sahoo. In this article, we study the solutions of certain type over a totally real number field K K of the Diophantine equation x 2 = B ​ y p + C ​ z p x^{2}=By^{p}+Cz^{p} with prime exponent p p , where B B is an odd integer and C C is either an odd integer or C = 2 r C=2^{r} for r ∈ ℕ r\in\mathbb{N} .

arxiv-2303-08532.title: Instability of magnetic skyrmion strings induced by longitudinal spin currents
arxiv-2303-08532.creator: Shun Okumura, Volodymyr P. Kravchuk, Markus Garst
arxiv-2303-08532.description: Abstract It is well established that spin-transfer torques exerted by in-plane spin currents give rise to a motion of magnetic skyrmions resulting in a skyrmion Hall effect. In films of finite thickness or in three-dimensional bulk samples the skyrmions extend in the third direction forming a string.

arxiv-2306-17443.title: Calm local optimality for nonconvex-nonconcave minimax problems Thanks: The research of Ye is supported by NSERC. Zhang’s work is supported by National Science Foundation of China (No.12222106), Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (No. 2022B1515020082) and Shenzhen Science and Tech
arxiv-2306-17443.creator: Xiaoxiao Ma, Wei Yao, Jane J. Ye, Jin Zhang
arxiv-2306-17443.description: Abstract Nonconvex-nonconcave minimax problems have found numerous applications in various fields including machine learning. However, questions remain about what is a good surrogate for local minimax optimum and how to characterize the minimax optimality. Recently Jin, Netrapalli, and Jordan (ICML 2020) introduced a concept of local minimax point and derived optimality conditions for the smooth and unconstrained case.

arxiv-2310-19127.title: Unified Representation for Non-compositional and Compositional Expressions
arxiv-2310-19127.creator: Ziheng Zeng, Suma Bhat
arxiv-2310-19127.description: Abstract Accurate processing of non-compositional language relies on generating good representations for such expressions. In this work, we study the representation of language non-compositionality by proposing a language model, Pier , that builds on BART and can create semantically meaningful and contextually appropriate representations for English potentially idiomatic expressions (PIEs).

arxiv-2312-02305.title: Effects of a Mixed Reality Headset on the Delay of Visually Evoked Potentials
arxiv-2312-02305.creator: Víctor Manuel Hidalgo, Carlos Andrés Bazaes, Juan-Carlos Letelier
arxiv-2312-02305.description: Abstract Virtual and mixed reality (VR, MR) technologies offer a powerful solution for on-the-ground flight training curricula. While these technologies offer safer and cheaper instructional programs, it is still unclear how they impact neuronal brain dynamics. Indeed, MR simulations engage students in a strange mix of incongruous visual, somatosensory and vestibular sensory input.

arxiv-2312-06882.title: Vertical shear instability in two-moment radiation-hydrodynamical simulations of irradiated protoplanetary disks
arxiv-2312-06882.creator: Julio David Melon Fuksman, Mario Flock, Hubert Klahr
arxiv-2312-06882.description: Abstract Context. Hydrodynamical instabilities are likely the main source of turbulence in weakly ionized regions of protoplanetary disks. Among these, the vertical shear instability (VSI) stands out as a rather robust mechanism due to its few requirements to operate, namely a baroclinic stratification, which is enforced by the balance of stellar heating and radiative cooling, and short thermal relaxation timescales.

arxiv-2404-05258.title: Unsupervised Band Selection Using Fused HSI and LiDAR Attention Integrating With Autoencoder
arxiv-2404-05258.creator: Judy X Yang, Jun Zhou, Jing Wang, Hui Tian, and Alan Wee Chung Liew
arxiv-2404-05258.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Judy X Yang, Jun Zhou, Jing Wang, Hui Tian, and Alan Wee Chung Liew. Band selection in hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is critical for optimising data processing and enhancing analytical accuracy. Traditional approaches have predominantly concentrated on analysing spectral and pixel characteristics within individual bands independently. These approaches overlook the potential benefits of integrating multiple data sources, such as Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), and is further challenged by the limited availability of labeled data in HSI processing, which represents a significant obstacle.

Frasca, G. Gilmore, V. Kalari, A. Lanzafame, S. Randich, S. Van Eck, S. Zaggia L. O. Kerber O. J Katime Santrich
arxiv-2507-00800.description: Abstract The Carina Nebula is an active star-forming region with several open clusters rich in massive OB stars, thus making it an optimal target for studying stellar properties such as rotation for large samples of these early-type stars. We studied a sample of early-type stars probable members of the 8 open clusters in the Carina Complex.

pmc-10523208.title: Implementation of Machine Learning Applications in Health Care Organizations: Protocol for a Systematic Review of Empirical Studies
pmc-10523208.creator: Vittoria Ardito, Giulia Cappellaro, Amelia Compagni, Francesco Petracca, Luigi Maria Preti, Amaryllis Mavragani, Huan-Wei Liang, David Kohen
pmc-10523208.description: BackgroundAn increasing interest in machine learning (ML) has been observed among scholars and health care professionals. However, while ML-based applications have been shown to be effective and have the potential to change the delivery of patient care, their implementation in health care organizations is complex.

pmc-10663982.title: Letter to the Editor: “Adverse Events and Subsequent Management Associated With Eustachian Tube Balloon Dilation”
pmc-10663982.creator: Aashish Batheja, Daniel H Coelho
pmc-10663982.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). omplications of BDET will better inform clinical decision‐making. 1 On May 8, 2023, we searched the MAUDE database for medical device reports involving BDET (indicated by product code “PNZ”) and gathered data on reported events and associated complications. Our independent investigation supports the major conclusions of Jeoung et al while offering additional clinical context and discussion of an adverse event reported after their search period.

pmc-11367885.title: Differences in the landscape of colonized microorganisms in different oral potentially malignant disorders and squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-group comparative study
pmc-11367885.creator: Xuan Zhou, Xinjia Cai, Qian Tang, Jianyun Zhang, Jiaying Bai, Fengyang Jing, Li Gao, Heyu Zhang, Tiejun Li
pmc-11367885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe role of microbes in diseases, especially cancer, has garnered significant attention. However, research on the oral microbiota in oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) remains limited. Our study investigates microbial communities in OPMDs.Materials and methodsOral biopsies from19 oral leukoplakia (OLK) patients, 19 proliferative verrucous leukoplakia (PVL) patients, 19 oral lichen planus (OLP) patients, and 19 oral lichenoid lesions (OLL) patients were obtained. 15 SCC specimens were also collected from PVL patients.

pmc-11461608.title: Adverse childhood experiences and profiles of healthy orthorexia versus orthorexia nervosa: towards an explanatory model of orthorexia as a multidimensional eating style
pmc-11461608.creator: Marcin Rzeszutek, Joanna Kowalkowska, Małgorzata Dragan, Katarzyna Schier, Maja Lis-Turlejska, Paweł Holas, Katarzyna Drabarek, Angelika Van Hoy, Dominika Maison, Gabriela Wdowczyk, Elżbieta Litwin, Julia Wawrzyniak, Wiktoria Znamirowska, Szymon Szumiał, Małgorzata Desmond
pmc-11461608.description: BackgroundOrthorexia is a complex phenomenon comprising distinct dimensions, including orthorexia nervosa (ON) and healthy orthorexia (HO). However, little is known about the factors influencing these dimensions, their disparities, and the psychological factors underlying orthorexia behaviours.ObjectivesThis study aims to explore ON versus HO dimensions and the predictive role of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) in a nationally representative sample of Polish individuals.

pmc-11505591.title: The Role of Immune Cells and Signaling Pathways in Diabetic Eye Disease: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-11505591.creator: Vincenzo Barone, Pier Luigi Surico, Francesco Cutrupi, Tommaso Mori, Gabriele Gallo Afflitto, Antonio Di Zazzo, Marco Coassin
pmc-11505591.description: Diabetic eye disease (DED) encompasses a range of ocular complications arising from diabetes mellitus, including diabetic retinopathy, diabetic macular edema, diabetic keratopathy, diabetic cataract, and glaucoma. These conditions are leading causes of visual impairments and blindness, especially among working-age adults. Despite advancements in our understanding of DED, its underlying pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

pmc-12597133.title: Mechanisms of lncRNA in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Wound Healing
pmc-12597133.creator: Yiming Chen, Mengting Wang, Xiaoliang Cao, Shengfeng Gao, Yasu Jiang, Zhenhua Gong
pmc-12597133.description: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic metabolic disease, and some diabetic patients develop diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), which are one of the most prevalent and serious complications among diabetic patients. These ulcers can lead to neuropathy, vasculopathy and severe infections.

pmc-12620589.title: Hypercholesterolemia as a Causal Risk Factor for COPD: Biomarker Discovery and Therapeutic Implications From NHANES Data
pmc-12620589.creator: Lu Liu, Chaoling Wu, Zhiyan Zhang, Xinxing Jin, Qi Zou, Mingxue Wang, Bo Huang, Xin Gan, Jianlin Tong
pmc-12620589.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), the third leading cause of global mortality, imposes substantial socioeconomic burdens. Existing therapies, such as smoking cessation and non-invasive ventilation, primarily alleviate symptoms without arresting disease progression. Comorbidities, including cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome, exacerbate functional decline, yet the causal role of dyslipidemia in COPD pathogenesis remains unclear.

pmc-13185153.title: PHYCUT: Scalable Multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 Editing for Genome Engineering in the Diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum
pmc-13185153.creator: Emily E. Stuckless, Lian S. Gai, Samuel S. Slattery, Kira H. Dempsey, Tyler S. Browne, Gregory B. Gloor, David R. Edgell
pmc-13185153.description: Diatoms are globally significant microalgae that contribute ∼20% of oxygen production and exhibit remarkable metabolic diversity. The marine diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum has emerged as a promising synthetic biology platform for the bioproduction of recombinant proteins, supported by a human-like N-linked glycosylation pathway. However, its α­(1,3)-linked core fucose is potentially immunogenic in humans and thus limits its biopharmaceutical applications.

pmc-13230718.title: Genome concatenation enables accurate dual RNA-seq mapping for lignocellulolytic fungi in coculture
pmc-13230718.creator: Bruna Pena Sollero, Rutiane Moreira de Jesus Costa, Roberto Coiti Togawa, Érica de Castro Costa, Robert Neil Gerard Miller
pmc-13230718.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dual RNA-seq enables simultaneous transcriptome profiling of interacting organisms, yet accurate read assignment remains challenging, particularly in fungal cocultures where phylogenetic proximity and high percentages of homologous sequences can be shared. Here, we evaluate two mapping strategies for dual RNA-seq analysis of Trichoderma reesei RUT-C30 and Pleurotus citrinopileatus cocultivated on sugarcane bagasse, based on a sequential alignment against individual genomes and a concatenated reference genome approach. Illumina NovaSeq sequencing generated 175 million high-quality reads, with mapping rates exceeding 96% across all strategies.

pmc-13267750.title: Ensilication preserves high-molecular weight native DNA for clinical long-read sequencing
pmc-13267750.creator: Alexis Ferrasse, Rodrigo Mendez, John E Gorzynski, Chloe Reuter, Jennefer N Carter, Michael Blas, Undiagnosed Diseases Network, Jonathan A Bernstein, Matthew T Wheeler, James L Banal, Euan A Ashley

pmc-13296611.title: mTOR Substrate Phosphorylation in Growth Control: An Update
pmc-13296611.creator: Don Benjamin, Michael N. Hall
pmc-13296611.description: Simple SummarymTOR is a central signaling hub that senses diverse inputs relating to cellular energy levels and nutrient status to coordinate cell metabolism and growth appropriately based on these input levels. The wide range of processes controlled by mTOR presupposes a befittingly large number of target proteins.

pmc-13350203.title: Routine intraoperative infection testing in presumed aseptic hip and knee revision: a matched cohort retrospective study
pmc-13350203.creator: Mattia Loppini, Caterina Rocchi, Marco Di Maio, Katia Chiappetta, Alberto Bulgarelli, Guido Grappiolo
pmc-13350203.description: Introduction Periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) complicate 1–2% of primary and up to 4% of revision arthroplasties, and their diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of a diagnostic gold standard. Differentiating PJI from aseptic failure is particularly difficult in low-grade or biofilm-related infections. Routine intraoperative microbiological screening is not recommended in presumed aseptic revisions.

pmc-13358801.title: Hydroxychloroquine Retinopathy in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Risk Factors, Screening, and Emerging Biomarkers
pmc-13358801.creator: Yehya Tlaiss, Ali Harajli, Ehab Al Mashtoub, Atef Salame Nasreddine, Tony Badawi, Alaa Tarchichi, Mohamad Tlais, Shweta Negi
pmc-13358801.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is a cornerstone therapy for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) because of its immunomodulatory and anti‐inflammatory benefits. However, long‐term exposure can cause HCQ‐induced retinopathy, a potentially irreversible adverse effect in which early detection is critical.
